The river rose twice that week (sample)

The bar sits above the outlined block and names it. Tab into the bar, then ← and → move between Around it, Inside it and Pin. In the hover cell the pointer rests on the page's words beside the bar, so the bar fades to half; point at the bar itself and it comes back. Turn off With words to see a block with no words of its own.

Field notes · October

Autumn at the footbridge

What we found at the footbridge, and what to do before winter.

The river

The river rose twice that week, and both times the footbridge held. The second rise came within a hand of the deck boards, which is closer than any year since the bridge was rebuilt.

Paragraph We recommend raising the deck

We recommend raising the deck by one course before the spring melt. The cost is modest and the work can be done in two days with the water low.

The path

The path on the north bank is washed out for about twenty metres. Walkers are cutting across the meadow, which is doing more harm than the river did.

Prompt to build this component

When to use it

When to use

  • In comment mode, around the block the pointer is over or the one just clicked: it outlines the block and names it by what it is and its own words, with three icons to move the comment around it, inside it, or turn it into a pin.

When not to use

  • For text selections: they get the selection's comment icon, not a bar.
  • As a label on content outside comment mode: nothing of Pipeup's shows on the page then.
Variants, anatomy, accessibility, interaction and content rules

Variants

Not applicable: one look. To add variants, replace this line with one bullet per variant, each a variant id, a dash and what it is for.

Anatomy

Built from:

  • cmp-icon-button, variant quiet — the three actions in the bar: Around it (caret-up), Inside it (caret-down) and Pin (push-pin), each named with aria-label.

Own parts:

  • Root: <div class="ds-naming-bar">, wrapping the picked block.
  • ds-naming-bar__bar: the bar above the block, a thin strip of paper with an ink edge, holding the name and the icons; role="toolbar" with an aria-label that repeats the name.
  • ds-naming-bar__kind: what the block is, in the typewriter face ("Paragraph", "Button", "Image").
  • ds-naming-bar__words (with-words): the block's own first words after a dot, cut to one line.
  • ds-naming-bar__target: the block itself, drawn with a dashed ink outline that never changes the block's size or place.

Accessibility

  • The bar is a toolbar: Tab reaches it, ← and → move between its three buttons, each with a name that says the action, never the glyph.
  • The outline is drawn outside the block, so the page's layout and the block's own focus ring are untouched.
  • The name is also read out when the block is chosen from the keyboard.

Interaction

  • The bar and the outline glide from the block last outlined to this one: position and size ease over --ds-motion-settle on --ds-motion-ease; the bar fades in the same way (int-04).
  • Hovering the bar keeps it fully opaque; while the pointer rests on the page's words right beside it, the bar fades to half over --ds-motion-quick so the words can be read (int-01).
  • The icons answer hover and press with colour only (int-03); focus shows the shared ring (int-02).
  • Under reduced motion the bar and outline appear in place (int-06).
  • The bar arrives and leaves with a fade over --ds-motion-settle: it carries data-ds-arriving for one frame and data-ds-leaving until it is hidden.

Content rules

  • The kind is one word in sentence case: "Paragraph", "Heading", "Table", "Button". A block with no words is a "Bar" or a "Shape".
  • The words are the block's own, up to about 40 characters, then an ellipsis.

Do and don't

  • Do keep the bar above the block, never over the block's own words.
  • Don't put words on the three actions; their names are in their labels and tooltips.
  • Don't let the outline change the page's layout.
